## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bhāgineyyupālittheraapadāna* ("Apadāna of the Elder Bhāgineyya-Upāli") is a biographical poem preserved in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. Designated as Tha Ap 43, it records the past deeds and spiritual attainment of the elder Bhāgineyya Upāli [SuttaCentral]. On SuttaCentral, the text is listed with modern translations into five languages [SuttaCentral].
No formal parallels are recorded on SuttaCentral, but automated analysis by DharmaNexus reveals extensive textual reuse within the Pali canon, identifying 185 matching passages shared across 27 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most substantial reuse partners are the two volumes of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* (49 matches with the *Paṭhamo bhāgo* and 37 matches with the *Dutiyo bhāgo*), reflecting the commentary's integration of the elder's biographical verses [DharmaNexus]. It also exhibits formulaic shared passages with numerous other *Therāpadāna* texts, notably the *Mogharājattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 37), *Raṭṭhapālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 20), *Kāḷudāyittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 36), and *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8) [DharmaNexus]. Outside Pali, DharmaNexus automatically aligns one passage (§17.4) with the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-ānandagarbhāvakrāntinirdeśa* (D0057) at a low plausibility score of 25 [DharmaNexus].
Direct discussions of this specific text are absent from the queried secondary literature, where occurrences of the search pattern represent false matches with footnote numbers or alternate numbering systems [Endo 1997; Jennings 1948; Walters].
